prompt:
Scene:
A square photograph at late morning with a 35mm full-frame camera, positioned on a cliff edge looking across a vast canyon. Warm sunlight, deep shadows in the canyon walls, visible atmospheric dust suggesting 2000-meter depth.

Subject:
A massive natural arch formed entirely of translucent smoky quartz spans from one cliff to another, roughly 1500 meters across. The arch is a single crystal body, twisted slightly as if grown rather than cut, with visible growth striations running along its length. Sunlight passes through the crystal and projects amber caustic patterns onto the canyon walls below.

Important details:
Authentic smoky quartz color graduation: darker in the thickest section, lighter at the tapered ends. Real surface micro-texture — crystal faces combined with partially conchoidal fractures at contact points. Two tiny climbers in bright yellow gear traverse the midpoint on ropes for scale. Hot air rising from the canyon floor creates subtle heat shimmer distorting the view of the bridge's underside.

Use case:
Crystal-studies single 2/5 — impossible monolithic crystal arch as landscape feature.

Constraints:
No readable text, no watermark, no logos, preserve exact 1:1 aspect ratio, no visible supports or cables, no contemporary brand gear (generic mountaineering only), no fantasy overlay, no cartoon.
